segmenti.tekst: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

After the king had his dream, and both he and the great dignitaries around him were unable to interpret that dream for him, the young man who had been with Yusuf remembered that there was a man there in the dungeon who interpreted dreams.
The dream in which the king saw seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean cows, by seven lean cows, and seven dried-up ears of grain eating, or destroying, seven green ears.

And Yusuf interpreted it: that these are seven years. First there will come, he says, seven fertile years, when people will reap; they will be fertile years, full of barakah (blessing), and people will store the food in the ears, not taking the grains out of the ears, but storing them that way so that the food would not spoil.

And that after that there will come seven severe years of drought, in which people will eat what they stored during those first seven blessed years. And after that, Yusuf says, there will come a year in which there will be much rain, much fruit, and so on, and so forth. Since the king had been very worried about this dream, he liked this interpretation of the dream, Yusuf's interpretation. So he sent an envoy to the prison to bring Yusuf.
And the malik, the king, said: "Bring me," he says, "Yusuf, bring him to me." And when the envoy came to Yusuf, came to the prison,

he said: "The king is summoning you to come to him at the palace." Yusuf said: "No, no, I will not go." For Yusuf, his honour was dearer than his freedom here. And this should be a lesson for the believer: that his honour should be dearer to him than freedom, than position, and than everything else.
So, honour first, and then the rest. What does Yusuf say to him, to this envoy? "Irji' ila rabbika" – he says: "Go back to your master, go back to your master,

fas'alhu ma balun-niswatil-lati qatta'na aydiyahunn. Ma balun-niswatil-lati qatta'na aydiyahunn" – "What about those women who cut their hands when I came in to them? Truly, my Lord knows well their schemes."
It is interesting that Yusuf did not mention the prime minister's wife, the governor's wife, but mentioned these women who had tried to lure him into fornication, who had invited him to fornication.

The scholars say: because of the kindness, it is said, that they had shown him when he was small, because of that kindness, since they had also raised him. "Akrimi mathwahu" – when he said, in this way, when this prime minister said: "Treat him well," he says.

"Make his stay here, in this palace, a pleasant one." And Yusuf did not forget that. Yusuf did not want to say: "Ask the king about so-and-so, why she put me in prison, why the prime minister put me in prison, because of this and that"; rather, because of that kindness towards him, he did not want to express himself that way.
So look, dear brothers, how Yusuf here respected those who had raised him.

So imagine how a person should respect, respect his own parents. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says that his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness and fed him for two years, nursed him for two years.

How grateful a person should be to his parents! And when Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentions kindness to parents, that command comes immediately after worshipping Him, that is, after the command to worship Him alone.

"وَقَضَى رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ" – and your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. "وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا" – and He says: that you treat your parents well, that you treat your parents well.

So Yusuf says here… here he did not, did not want to… but this was very clever and shrewd of Yusuf, because Yusuf knew that the king would get to the bottom of it, and that the king would find out, through his own channels, who had tried to lure him into fornication, who had sent him to prison, and so on, and so forth.

So after that the king gathered these women, and of course among them this wife of the prime minister, and said: "Qala ma khatbukunna" – the king said: "What is the matter with you," he says, "what is the matter with you – idh rawadtunna Yusufa – why did you invite Yusuf to fornication? Did he give you any cause? Did Yusuf give you any cause?" "All that we have heard about him has been good."

Then the wife of this prime minister spoke up, after she realised that Yusuf had not once spoken ill of her. And the Qur'an tells us this: from beginning to end, Yusuf did not once speak ill of her, neither in prison, nor before, nor after.
So she says: if this man is so chaste and good, then the truth must come out, the truth must come to light. It cannot be otherwise.

Now the truth will come to light. "Ana rawadtuhu 'an nafsihi" – she says: "It was I who invited him," she says, "to fornication. It was I who invited him to fornication. Wa innahu la minas-sadiqin" – "and he," she says, "was telling the truth," that is, he would not respond to my invitation. He would not respond to my invitation.

And Yusuf too – we mentioned yesterday – that he was, well, one of the siddiqin, those who always speak the truth, the truthful, those who love the truth. And she says: "I have also said this so that my husband knows that I did not betray him" – by inventing lies about him – that I did not commit immorality with Yusuf, but that it all came down to an invitation to zina.

That neither I nor he crossed the line and committed fornication. "And that Allah," she says, "will never guide the betrayers." Allah will not guide a treacherous person, and He will not allow, will not allow his treachery and his schemes to find their way to innocent, pure people. Allah will not allow it,

however possible it may sometimes seem to us. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, [unclear] that their schemes always come back upon whom? Upon them. This woman further says: "Wa ma ubarri'u nafsi" – she says: "I do not absolve myself."

She says: "Truly, truly," she says, "the soul, truly the soul," she says, "incites a person to evil." That is the basis: that the soul incites a person to evil. And there are three kinds of soul. The first is "ammaratun bis-su'," as Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentions here in the Qur'an, the one that constantly incites a person to evil.
The soul that reproaches itself is the second kind. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "And I swear by the self-reproaching soul."

And this one has two sub-types. There is the soul that reproaches itself when a person commits some bad deed; it reproaches him and says: "You could have done a good deed, why did you do a bad deed?" And, it is said, there is the one that leads a person astray and reproaches him when he does some good deed. So it happens that a person gives five euros in charity, and it says: "You could have given a hundred dinars, [unclear] five euros, that's a lot, you don't have that much to keep giving away." And that really is how it is, dear brothers.

Here, examine yourselves and you will see. And the third is "an-nafsul-mutma'innah" (the soul at peace). [unclear] Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, [unclear] in the Qur'an: "Ya ayyatuhan-nafsul-mutma'innah, irji'i ila Rabbiki radiyatan mardiyyah" – [unclear] – "fadkhuli fi 'ibadi" – enter among My servants – "wadkhuli jannati" – and enter My Jannah (Paradise). [unclear] Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, when the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, passed away, he… kissed him. After that, after he had passed away, he recited
these ayat. Also, dear brothers, it is mentioned there, it is said, that a person's three greatest enemies are: this soul that incites a person to evil, Shaytan, and a bad friend.

There is no greater enemy for a person than a bad friend. You will see that a person is on the right path, and comes to the mosque, and loves his neighbours, and is dutiful to his parents, obedient, and obedient to Allah, and then he starts keeping company with bad people… And, as the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), says, a person remains, or ends up, upon the religion of his friend. That is the saying: tell me who your friends are, and I will tell you who you are.

It cannot be otherwise. A person cannot be good and have bad friends, or the other way round. Not at all. Rather, only if you are good will you have good friends. If you are good, you will leave those bad friends. That is all for today. In sha Allah, we will continue tomorrow. May Allah grant you every good.
